challenges.claim_challenged: RG-C-019 max_age_extension_seconds counted as a manageable (eligible, COUPLED) parameter.
challenges.finding: DR-CP-AGE-1 decision 5 (accepted) already assigns the composition of this exact field: max_age_extension_seconds := min(original, min over classes max(0, ceiling_c - narrowed_base_c)) in a later host factory EXT-S3-4. A second, stand-alone Registry slot would create two narrowing sources for one field. Worker A said do not count as an independent parameter; the lead's own blocking_decision text says 'decide whether a separate Registry slot is needed or the derivation suffices', which by the audit's own BLOCKED rule (open Architect decision) is not ELIGIBLE. Lead recorded only a sensitivity (-1).
challenges.evidence: dr-cp-age-1.md decision 5 (line 23); parameter-catalogue P-RG-C-019 blocking_decision; A.jsonl summary disagreements; freshness.py:67-68
challenges.suggested_correction: Reclassify as derived from LR-F5 (not a separate parameter; manageable 19, rules 12) or BLOCKED pending the Architect choice; keep the +/-1 in the headline range, not only in the sensitivity table.

challenges.claim_challenged: P-RG-D-027-tier_delay_ceilings: owner 'Constitutional-authority document (derived from the constitution ...)', evidence quoting 'derived from the constitution'; counted as a BLOCKED configurable parameter.
challenges.finding: The source says the opposite. authority_context.py:12-15: 'Proposed per-tier ceilings ... Owner to confirm: no value is validated or derived from the constitution.' The quoted evidence drops the negation. The constant lives in testing/harness/authority_context.py whose module docstring is 'Local reference checks only. No credentials, network, grants or effects.' and it is referenced only by tests. So the Worker A dissent (constitutional invariant) is not supported by source, and 'BLOCKED' on a consuming boundary is the wrong frame: the unit is a harness constant, consistent with how the audit treated D-021/D-022 (OUT-OF-SCOPE reference code). It also inflates the denominator (81) and blocked count (4).
challenges.suggested_correction: Correct the evidence/owner text; classify RG-D-027 tier ceilings OUT-OF-SCOPE (reference harness) or UNRESOLVED(owner confirm); denominator 80, blocked 3 (or leave BLOCKED but fix the misquote and drop the 'constitutional' framing). Remove the A-dissent sentence or mark it contradicted.

challenges.claim_challenged: Consistent rationale for ELIGIBLE (terminal-revocation, C-010, C-020) vs non-manageable (operation-identity enablement 'a Registry record that later disappears would silently revert to off').
challenges.finding: The 'disappearing record reverts to host baseline' objection applies to every Registry narrowing (F1a withdrawal returns the caller policy) and is not what distinguishes op-identity (a 3-way protocol selection that changes identity semantics, not a strictness-only toggle). The lead's text should state the actual distinguishing test (strictness-only, one-way, profile adds only refusals) so TR/C-010/C-020 versus op-identity is principled. All 10 non-governed eligible parameters carry an open blocking_decision (AUD-D06 / M11 6.A,6.E / 60-vs-300) yet are ELIGIBLE, while RG-C-005/006 with an open Architect decision are BLOCKED; the difference (prior contrary decision vs open design question) is not stated.
challenges.evidence: lead-adjudications pass2_resolutions (NEW:operation-identity-enablement, G-01); parameter-catalogue blocking_decision fields
challenges.suggested_correction: State the ELIGIBLE/BLOCKED test in the method section: BLOCKED = an accepted decision conflicts; ELIGIBLE = design gate only.

challenges.claim_challenged: P-RG-C-011-reversibility defined as 'ActionClass.reversibility' rank parameter, consumer reversibility.py:165-181.
challenges.finding: A Registry cannot force reversibility='irreversible' without the reversibility/0.1 profile: runtime_authority.py (model_validator _profiles_compose) raises 'reversibility values need the reversibility/0.1 profile' for any declared class, and the lead's own text says a Registry must never enable that profile. The profile-free monotone lever is the legacy ActionClass.irreversible bool (default True; consumers bounded.py:2111,2189, reversibility.py:179-181 effectively_irreversible), which the catalogue records only as invariant I-W8-004. The eligible parameter is therefore mis-specified; confidence LOW is honest, but the rule-level confidence (MEDIUM) and 'REGISTRY-ELIGIBLE' headline overstate it.
challenges.suggested_correction: Re-specify C-011 as the one-way False->True of ActionClass.irreversible (no profile) or demote to UNRESOLVED; align rule confidence to LOW.
